newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber rises on government intervention news.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber rises on government intervention news.

text.p: Thai rubber prices rose this week, lifted by tighter supplies and news of government intervention to prop up prices, but demand remained slow, trade sources said on Wednesday.
A government official told Reuters that the cabinet on Tuesday approved the measures to support local rubber prices, which included price intervention and providing loans to promote exports.
Under the scheme, the state-run Rubber Estate Organization would buy RSS3 grade rubber at 27.50 baht a kg ($1.05) from 25.00 baht previously.
The government would also provide one billion baht of soft loans for operating funds and 1.5 billion baht for export supporting funds through the REO.
"The demand has not picked up much from last week. Buying was mostly from Japan," said a Hat Yai trader.

"It's the government measures which is expected to push up the offer prices and the tighter supplies that will boost prices. Anyway, I don't know how long this uptrend can last given slow demand," he said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for April delivery was quoted around 122.50 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok from 121-122 cents last week. Concentrated latex also edged up to 94 cents a kg from 93 cents a week earlier.
